This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
S.G. Pandit J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The claimant/injured is in appeal being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under the judgment and award dated 01.04.2016, passed in M.V.C.No.222/2015 on the file of the VI Additional District and Sessions Judge & Additional M.A.C.T., at Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal'),
and praying for enhancement of compensation.
2. Heard learned counsel Sri.Vitthal S. Teli., for the appellant-claimant, and learned counsel Sri.Rajesh B. Rajnal for respondent No.2-insurance company.
Perused the appeal papers and Tribunal records.

3. It is stated that the claimant/injured filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, '1988 Act') claiming compensation for the accidental injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident that occurred on 05.05.2014 involving Tata Sumo bearing registration No.KA-22-P-6875.
It is the case of the claimant that claimant/injured suffered three fractures and she was inpatient for 13 days.
The injured was aged 50 years as on the date of the accident and she claims that she was earning Rs.10,000/- per month from agriculture.
4. On service of notice, respondent No.2 appeared and filed objections.

Respondent No.2-insurance company denied the claim petition averments and also contended that the respondent No.1 - owner of the vehicle has carried more than 15 passengers for hire and reward on the offending vehicle as against the permitted capacity, which amounts to violation of terms and conditions of the policy.

5. The Tribunal on consideration of the material on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.3,35,000/- on the following heads:
 Sl

Particulars Amount  1. Pain and sufferings Rs.30,000/-

2 . Loss of future happiness and amenities Rs.50,000/-
 3. Loss of income during the treatment Rs.21,000/-
 period  4. Incidental charges Rs.21,000/-

 Total Rs.3,35,000/-
While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed the income of the claimant/injured at Rs.7,000/- per month and assessed the whole body disability at 15% as against the evidence of the Doctor at 25% and adopted the multiplier '13'.
6.

sentences.text: Learned counsel, Sri.Vitthal S. Teli., for the claimant/injured would contend that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal when compared to the injuries sustained by the claimant/injured is meager.

Further, learned counsel would submit that income of the claimant/injured assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is on the lower side and he submits that the claimant was earning Rs.10,000/- per month by doing agricultural work.
The Tribunal ought to have assessed the income of the claimant on the higher side.

Further, learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal committed error in assessing whole body disability at 15% as against the evidence of the Doctor that the claimant suffers 25% whole body disability.

Further,
learned counsel would submit that claimant had suffered three fractures.
The claimant/injured not being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation is before this Court seeking enhancement.

7. On the other hand, Sri.Rajesh B. Rajnal, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2-insurance company would submit that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just compensation and requires no interference.
Further he submits that, to assess income of the claimant/injured, no cogent material is placed on record.
Hence, the Tribunal is justified in assessing the notional income of the claimant/injured at Rs.7,000/- per month.
Further, learned counsel would submit that compensation awarded on the other heads needs no interference.

Thus,
he prays for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the memorandum of appeal and the Trial Court Records, the only point which falls for our consideration is, "Whether the claimant/injured is entitled for enhanced compensation?"
9.

The answer to the above point would be in the affirmative for the following reasons:
10. The accident which took place on 05.05.2014 involving Tata Sumo bearing registration No.KA-22-P-6875 and the resultant injury suffered by the injured claimant is not in dispute, in this appeal.

sentences.text: 3  2) Right 1st to 6th rib fractures; and  3) Heamopneumothorax.

11. It is also not in dispute that the claimant/injured was inpatient for 13 days for the treatment and that it is also not in dispute that the claimant/injured was aged 50 years as on the date of the accident.

12. The Tribunal assessed the income of the claimant/injured at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the statement of the claimant that she was earning more than Rs.10,000/- per month by doing agricultural work.
To substantiate the claim made by the claimant/injured, she has not placed on record any cogent or acceptable documents to establish her exact income.
It is for the Court to assess income notionally.

In the absence of any material on record to establish the avocation and earning of the appellant/claimant, this Court and Lok Adalat while settling the accidental claims of the year 2014, normally would assess notional income at Rs.7,500/- per month, taking note of the chart prepared by KSLSA based on various factors including the minimum wage fixed.

In the instant case also, in the absence of any material evidence to establish the income of the injured, we are of the opinion that it would be appropriate for us to determine the income of the injured at Rs.7,500/- p.m., taking note of the income chart prepared by KSLSA.
13. The claimant has examined the Doctor in support of her claim with regard to disability.
The Doctor examined on behalf of the claimant/appellant has stated that the claimant suffers from 25% permanent physical disability.
The 25% permanent physical disability stated by the Doctor is with regard to a particular limb.
When the disability to a particular limb is stated by the Doctor, the Tribunal would normally assess the physical disability at 1/3rd of the disability to a particular limb.

Therefore,
the assessment of physical disability at 15% made by the Tribunal is proper and correct, which needs no interference.

Thus, the claimant/injured would be entitled to compensation on the head of loss of future income at Rs.1,75,500/- (Rs.7,500 X 12 X 13 X 15%).
14.
The compensation awarded on the other heads by the Tribunal is on the lower side when compared to the fractures sustained by the claimant and also treatment taken as inpatient for 13 days.
The claimant injured has suffered three fractures.

Therefore, the compensation awarded at Rs.30,000/- on the head pain and sufferings is on the lower side and in addition to Rs.30,000/-, the claimant would be entitled for another Rs.45,000/- on the said head.
15. The compensation of Rs.50,000/- awarded on the head 'loss of future happiness and amenities' is also on the lower side when compared to the fractures and treatment taken.

Therefore, in addition to Rs.50,000/-, claimant/injured would be entitled to another Rs.25,000/-

4 on the said head.

Loss of income during the laid up period is taken at rate of Rs.7,500/- per month,
which would come to Rs.22,500/-.
16. The compensation awarded on the heads incidental charges and medical expenses, which according to us are just and proper and the same is not disturbed.

17. Thus, the claimant would be entitled to modified compensation as under:
- 10 - Sl.No. Particulars Amount  1. Pain and sufferings Rs.75,000/-
 2. Loss of future happiness and Rs.75,000/-
 amenities  3. Loss of income during the Rs.22,500/-
 treatment period  4.

Incidental charges Rs.21,000/-

Medical expenses Rs.49,200/-

Thus, the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,18,200/- as against Rs.3,35,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
19. Hence, we pass the following order.
ORDER  a) The appeal is allowed in part.

b) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.4,18,200/- as against Rs.3,35,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per - 11 - annum from the date of petition till date of payment.
